meta.descrizione: A pixel-art action platformer, in development. Taranto, 2087: the arm comes with a subscription, revenge doesn’t. Play the demo in your browser.

eroe.tocco: Play it on a computer: keyboard or gamepad.

storia.nota: In the game, the story is told by Totò’s murals. These panels are illustrations made for the site with the game’s real art: the mural style is still being tested.

cartelloni.testo: White domes cover the old steelworks: beneath them, so they say, SIDERA’s great clean-up is under way, and by Easter the city will finally be pure.

Cataldo Gigante, GIG to everyone, is the engineer from the Tamburi district who designed MANODOPERA, the cybernetic arm that gave injured workers back the arm they had lost on the job, and which SIDERA now rents out by subscription.

After the death of Mimmo, his oldest friend, GIG asked too many questions: within a week he had lost his job, his home and his name on the patents, and his arm was locked remotely with two words: “Subscription expired.”
As the perdoni, hooded and barefoot, file out of the Carmine church, two Esattori, SIDERA’s repo men, track him down at Mimmo’s grave in San Brunone cemetery to repossess the arm.

GIG escapes to his mother’s garage, plugs his father’s old keyboard into the arm and hits <kbd>CTRL</kbd>+<kbd>ALT</kbd>+<kbd>CANC</kbd> (CANC is Delete on Italian keyboards), two keys with his one good hand and the third with his nose:

the arm reboots and starts to talk, his eye turns cyan, and with his first double jump his single night begins, that afternoon, on the rooftops of the Tamburi, where his guide is Totò, eleven years old, who sprays REVENGE on the walls.

storia.errore_label: The MANODOPERA window: subscription expired. Next to it, GIG’s portrait with his cyber eye switched off.
storia.tasti_aiuto: Press all three, like GIG: two with your good hand, the third with your nose.
storia.ritratto_spento: GIG, his cyber eye switched off.
storia.ritratto_acceso: GIG, his cyber eye switched on: it’s cyan.

mondo.sotto: Taranto, 2087: the world of the game
paragrafi: Since 2041 the old steelworks has been sealed under white domes marked “Construction site, no entry”. SIDERA calls it the clean-up, and has given it a name that sounds like a streaming service: ARIA+, “The air you deserve” (aria means air), with ARIA+ Premium for those who can pay. A red cloud hangs over the city: the smoke, they say, is “clean-up steam”, the dust a “temporary inconvenience”. The Colombe (“doves”), white drones carrying the ARIA+ logo, measure the air and spray a fresh, clean scent; they are named after the wooden dove that tradition credits to Archytas, the engineer-philosopher of Greek Taranto. On the big screens, the Easter celebration is already being advertised: “Taranto is pure”.

The Tamburi is the working-class district pressed up against the steelworks: public housing blocks with small terraces, washing hung out to dry and turned red by the dust, windows stopped up with wet towels whenever the north-west wind blows the dust in. Everything that was once pale wears a red film, even the tombs of San Brunone cemetery. Above the streets runs the Linea (“the Line”): conveyor belts on concrete pylons that disappear under the domes. At the foot of the pylons stands Ignazio’s MiniBar, GIG’s local. Plenty of people here wear a MANODOPERA arm (the word means “workforce”, literally “the work of the hand”) with red rings, on a monthly subscription; miss a payment and the Esattori come knocking.

aria.label: A SIDERA advert, in the world of the game
aria.colombe: They measure the air. They smell squeaky clean. Here come the Colombe.
aria.clausola: ARIA+ Premium for those who can pay.

strada.label: The slice’s street, from the bar to the kebab shop: as you scroll, GIG walks along it towards two Esattori waiting for him.
strada.didascalia: A stretch of the slice’s street, with its own art and lights: scroll and GIG walks. It’s still a generic street, and we’ll rebuild it so it tells the story of the Tamburi.

notte.testo: It all happens in a single night, from Holy Thursday into Good Friday, 17–18 April 2087, which is also the city’s oldest night.

orari.cosa: the perdoni, barefoot and hooded, leave the Carmine church and walk from church to church to pray at the Altars of Repose, with the slow, rocking step called the nazzicata;
from San Domenico in the Old Town, the procession of Our Lady of Sorrows (the Addolorata) sets out, led by the troccolante and his wooden clapper, the troccola.

notte.chiusa: By 2087 almost everything in Taranto has changed, except this.

gioco.intro: A pixel-art action platformer, with combat arenas and hacking puzzles. This is the game we’re making: each pillar says what you can already try in the slice and what is still in development.

pilastri.titolo: Platforming and fights, in one night
pilastri.slice: running, a live cable to jump, and an arena fight that ends with ZONA LIBERATA (“zone cleared”).
pilastri.sviluppo: the double jump, and the camera tilting as the Esattori turn up.
pilastri.testo: You run and jump side-on in 2D, with a double jump from the moment the arm reboots, early in the prologue; when the Esattori turn up the camera tilts, the floor opens out and the fight moves into depth, like the side-scrolling arcade classics. When it’s over, VAI (“GO”) flashes up and you’re back to jumping.

pilastri.slice: jab, jab, cyber hook and kick; grabs with knee strikes and throws; the flying kick.
pilastri.sviluppo: a dodge into depth, a timed parry, the Scarica and things to throw.
pilastri.testo: The combo only continues if the blow connects: jab, jab, cyber hook, kick. Grabs with knee strikes and throws, where a thrown body bowls over anyone in the way, plus a flying kick. Coming next: a dodge into depth, a timed parry with the cyber arm that opens up a counter, the Scarica (an electric punch), and bins, pipes and crates to throw.

pilastri.sviluppo: the Spinta, ledge grabs, slides, wall jumps, air dashes, wall runs and the Rampino.
pilastri.testo: Run, variable-height jump and Spinta, a double jump kicked off by a downward blast from the arm; ledge grabs, slides, wall jumps, air dashes and wall runs. Later on, the Rampino, a grapple to swing from cables and chains like Pitfall’s vines. And the forgiving jump timing players expect today.

GIG plugs his arm into the SIDERA panels that his cyan eye, the Vista, reveals: he reverses the Linea’s belts, opens gates, reprograms the Colombe and switches off lasers. They’re timed hacking puzzles inside the level, Comix Zone style; the few biggest hacks get a full-screen mini-game, a data stream to route through a grid.

The Vista cuts through the red dust of the Wind Days, when the north-west wind blows hard over Taranto, to reveal fake walls, invisible platforms and ARIA+ billboards that, looked at properly, point the way. Every act hides arm logs, secret-hunting in the Duke Nukem and Jazz Jackrabbit tradition: each tells a worker’s story, and the more you find, the richer the epilogue. On the walls, Totò’s tags to collect.
At certain moments you choose what GIG says. There’s no meter on screen, but the story remembers, right up to the ending.

pilastri.titolo: Taranto you can play, with today’s rules
pilastri.testo: Real places, from San Brunone cemetery to the rooftops of the Tamburi, and the city’s own food as pick-ups: taralli, coffee from the MiniBar, panzerotti and the rare Easter scarcella, which pushes your health past the maximum. Three acts in a single night, a prologue and [[capitoli]] chapters, replayable for missed secrets; frequent checkpoints, unlimited retries and no GAME OVER, and for a thrill, an optional arcade mode with three lives and a CONTINUA? (“continue?”) screen.

demo.testo: The “Sotto la Linea” (“Under the Line”) slice plays in your browser, with a keyboard or a gamepad: from the title screen to the end of the demo, GIG against the punk and the brute. It has no music, because the tracks aren’t public.
demo.onesta: It’s the 2026 technical slice: the art, the text and the levels will change, the game’s own text is in Italian, and in the browser all sounds come from the centre. The first load downloads about [[demo_mb]] MB.

comandi.nota: A gamepad works too. Try pressing the keys: they light up here.

tecnica.sotto: Pixel art is the style, not a period limitation.
paragrafi: The game runs at 384×216 pixels, scaled up by whole multiples, and uses modern techniques wherever they look better. The slice already has dynamic lights with normal maps on the characters, sparks and particles, hit-stop on impacts and slow motion on the final KO; the full game can also use a smooth camera, shaders and deformation.

The comic-book scenes, meaning the intro and the interludes, are Totò’s murals: pixel art in a street-art style, with spray-can gradients, drips, thick outlines and neon colours. The camera pans along the wall and the panels come alive with parallax, lights and particles. The mural style is still being tested, and the look of the sprites may change too: everything here is work in progress.

This site follows the same rules: every pixel of the art is a game pixel, scaled up by a whole number of your screen’s pixels, and the cloud and the dust are drawn by the page’s own code, with old-school Bayer dithering.

luce.didascalia: GIG’s real sprite, with its normal map: move the pointer over the box, or use the arrow keys when it’s selected, and the light follows. Your browser computes it, the way Godot does in the game.
luce.label: GIG on guard, lit by a moving light: move it with the pointer or the arrow keys.

catena.titolo: How the art is made, at zero cost

passi.testo: The characters start from free 3D models and animations released under CC0, by Quaternius and Mesh2Motion.
Blender animates and renders them. The key moves, meaning the grab, knee strikes, throw, cyber hook and flying kick, are poses written into the scripts.
Python scripts turn them into pixel art, with a palette for each material, stamps for facial details, a springy ponytail, procedurally built boots and a normal map for every sprite sheet.

Backgrounds are procedural geometry and painting, with a handful of recoloured CC0 pieces and our own pixel typeface for the shop signs. Fonts, effects, interface and sound effects come from scripts too, with no samples or asset packs.
Godot puts it all together, with dynamic lights and fixed-tick logic.

catena.chiusa: No hand retouching, and no image generated by an AI: the scripts, written by AI agents for Luigi Massari, are deterministic, use fixed seeds and can all be read in the repository.

tappe.sotto: In development, November 2026. CTRL+ALT REVENGE is being rebuilt from scratch in Godot [[godot]], Windows first; the old Python/Pygame prototype is archived in the legacy-pygame branch.
tappe.prova: The score above is real: it comes from the demo replay the tests play back. With this version it always ends on tick [[tick]] with [[punteggio]] points and the same hash, [[hash]]…: the logic runs on fixed ticks and is deterministic, and the tests check it by playing the same replays twice. There are [[test]] groups of automated tests.

righe.testo: Written and approved from start to finish: prologue, three acts, ending and epilogue, with the comic-book intro and interludes.
Decided and written down: platforming and arenas, moves, combat, hacking puzzles, health and checkpoints, pick-ups, secrets, chapters and hazards.
Sourced research on Taranto, and a timeline that keeps places, dates, times, weather and even that night’s moon consistent.

Playable from the title screen to the end of the demo: GIG against the punk and the brute, with combos, grabs, knee strikes, throws, a flying kick, a live cable to jump and an arena that ends with ZONA LIBERATA. Version 7 sprites with normal maps and dynamic lights, synthesised sound effects, and fixed-tick game logic checked by automated tests and deterministic replays.
Plain grey, to fine-tune the moves: jumps, double jump, walls, dash, grapple and the switch to the arena with the tilting camera.
San Brunone cemetery and the garage, with the arm’s reboot.
“The Rooftops of the Tamburi”, with the first arm log, food pick-ups and the mural intro.
The style test for the murals, and the soundtrack, with a ’90s sound but not necessarily chiptune.

tappe.slice: The slice is a technical test, and its street is still generic. We’ll rebuild it so it shows Taranto on the evening of Holy Thursday 2087: the red cloud instead of a starry sky, wind and red dust instead of rain, the Linea’s conveyor belts instead of a railway, neighbourhood shop signs instead of anywhere-metropolis neon.

piede.finzione: CTRL+ALT REVENGE is a work of fiction, set in a Taranto of 2087 imagined from the real city. SIDERA, ARIA+, MANODOPERA and all the characters are invented, Ignazio included; the MiniBar sign is used with the owner’s permission. Any other resemblance to real people or companies is coincidental. The city’s places and rituals are real, and we portray them with respect.

contesto.testo: The story was written in November 2026, in the days when Taranto’s blast furnaces began to be shut down. The game doesn’t retell the news: it imagines Taranto sixty years on, and takes aim at those in power, never at the people who live there, work there or have fallen ill.
